instructions:
# Instructions

Refactor a Markdown parser.

The markdown exercise is a refactoring exercise.
There is code that parses a given string with [Markdown syntax][markdown] and returns the associated HTML for that string.
Even though this code is confusingly written and hard to follow, somehow it works and all the tests are passing!
Your challenge is to re-write this code to make it easier to read and maintain while still making sure that all the tests keep passing.

It would be helpful if you made notes of what you did in your refactoring in comments so reviewers can see that, but it isn't strictly necessary.
The most important thing is to make the code better!

[markdown]: https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax

/* Original C17 port of the MIT-licensed Exercism Python exercise.
 * Heap-allocated return values belong to the caller; release with free() or
 * the matching destroy/free function. Inputs and labels are borrowed unless
 * an initializer explicitly copies them. Initialize state structs to zero.
 * Caller output arrays must fit the complete result: at most the input element
 * count (flatten: all integer leaves), rows*columns (boards), 512 (Sudoku),
 * tree node count (paths), target/minimum_coin (change), or interval count+1 / 12 (scales). String outputs
 * without a size argument need strlen(input)+strlen(input)/5+1 bytes for
 * cipher encode, strlen(input)+1 for decode, and rows/4*(columns/3+1)+1 for OCR.
 */
#ifndef EXERCISE_H
#define EXERCISE_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
char *parse(const char *markdown);
#endif
